title: Pikachu Plush Visits the Space Station
summary:
A Pikachu plush has been to space! The European Space Agency, or ESA, shared the news on September 19, 2026. The toy spent 67 days on the International Space Station, or ISS.

Pikachu went there on a Cygnus cargo spacecraft on April 11. It returned to Earth on a SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft on June 17. While in orbit, it traveled around Earth about 1,040 times.

The trip was part of ESA's plans to celebrate World Space Week 2026, which runs from October 4 to 10. ESA made a special exhibit that mixes space science with Pokémon characters. It shows Europe's space missions and life on the ISS. Visitors can learn how ESA studies the Sun, the Solar System, and the wider universe.

The exhibit tour began at ESA headquarters in Paris, France, in late September. It will visit places across Europe through April 2027.

Pokémon GO players can join activities at participating science and space museums in Europe. These run from October 4, 2026, through April 30, 2027. They include One-Star Raids with Astronaut Pikachu, research tasks, and chances to encounter event-themed Pokémon.

ESA hopes the project will make children and teens curious about space and science. ESA Director General Josef Aschbacher said, "Inspiring future generations is a key part of ESA's mission."
why_it_matters: The exhibit connects a familiar character with information about space missions and life on the ISS. ESA hopes this will encourage children and teens to explore science.
